role: calibration: Balandraud's sharp subset-sum threshold quantifies the ω(N) shortfall
missing_theorem: (Calibration, known.) In ℤ/q (q prime) k distinct non-zero residues have ≥ min(q, k(k+1)/2 + 1) subset sums (Balandraud). Transferred via discrete logs to cyclic (ℤ/e)^× (order φ(e), usually composite, where subgroups break the bound), k = ω(N) ≈ log log p factors force a prescribed target only if φ(e) ≲ (log log p)²/2 — essentially bounded slices, which are a fixed menu (B2(iii)). Makes the B4 shortfall exact.
status_ref: Balandraud, Israel J. Math. 188 (2012) (theorem); LONGSHOT_PIGEONHOLE Prop 1.4; FRONTIER §3 B4, B2(iii)

role: Combinatorial Nullstellensatz for grid-restricted ES congruence solutions
missing_theorem: A grid-restricted solution of 4xyz ≡ n(xy + yz + zx) (mod ℓ) for many ℓ simultaneously, as a step to size-constrained integer solutions. Mod-ℓ solutions on grids exist trivially (local solvability free); passing from 'mod many ℓ with restricted coordinates' to an exact integer solution is the archimedean size cut (Z1694), which polynomial methods over F_ℓ do not see.
status_ref: FRONTIER §1 (BL Thm 1.8); out_Q11 Z1694; out_P05 Z2816; BRAINSTORM/polynomial_method.md
note: Known-true: local grid solutions exist. Why ES is not done: integrality at the exact height.

role: disproof-shape calibration: count divisor-closed failure sets avoiding identity coverage (hypergraph containers)
missing_theorem: (Calibration.) The ES failure set is closed under taking divisors (ES(d) ⇒ ES(n) for d | n) and lies in the uncovered classes of every identity menu; containers bound the number of such independent sets. This constrains possible failure-set shapes but cannot show the set is empty (the odd squares are never covered by identities, and T1 makes every identity-avoiding pattern realisable at squares).
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 'No BM obstruction / the shape of a disproof' ((J)97), B1 (identity menus never cover odd-square classes; out_P06 Z0391)
barrier: B1 (identity coverage is blind at squares), B6

role: ergodic sum-product Ramsey (Moreira, Hindman) forcing a mixed additive–multiplicative configuration
missing_theorem: A partition-regularity theorem whose monochromatic configurations include {p, C, 4Cp+1, d, (4Cp+1)/d} with d ≡ −1 (mod 4C) at a PRESCRIBED p. Ramsey/ergodic theorems produce configurations somewhere in every colouring (existence over ℕ, i.e. averages), never at a prescribed integer; at a fixed p the configuration is the divisor event.
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 B6 (no prescribed-integer content in density/ergodic statements); out_Q10 Z0135 (reciprocal Rado)
note: OAI 164 (Hindman sums and products) is CLAIMED; irrelevant either way at fixed p.

role: disproof-shape: algebraic pseudorandom constructions as candidate 'sterile' structures
missing_theorem: (Calibration.) Sterile residue patterns (profinite points sterile for finite slice menus, STERILE_EXPLICIT) are congruence objects that exist by B1/T1 logic; they are not counterexamples to ES (sterility is relative to finite menus, while every actual prime has certificates in the census). Algebraic incidence structures (Hermitian unitals) could at most give explicit sterile patterns, i.e. more B1 data.
status_ref: STERILE_EXPLICIT.md; FRONTIER §3 B1, §7.9 (r-generic sterile points), §7.15 ('prime T1' needed for a disproof)
